meta.document: Frontend Redesign Plan — Personal Financial Manager
meta.supersedes_nothing: docs/REBUILD_PLAN.json is COMPLETE. This is the next pass: a visual, structural and interaction redesign of the 9 screens that plan produced.

companion_documents.docs/AUDIT_AND_REBUILD_PLAN.md: prose audit + Appendix Z (execution findings). Z8, Z9, Z16 are still open there and are NOT restated here.

meta.goal_from_owner: Make the product visually good, colourful, attractive and interesting, and confirm that every screen, dialog, button, card, table and label earns its place and works.
meta.method: The real application was rendered offscreen under PyQt6 6.11 with QT_QPA_FONTDIR=C:/Windows/Fonts (174 font families, Segoe UI present — so unlike the previous audit, typography and layout in the captures are TRUSTWORTHY). All 9 screens and 10 dialogs were screenshotted and introspected; Excel shortcuts were exercised with QTest on every live table.

rules: Work in `recommended_sequence` order. Phases V1-V3 are foundation; screens (V6) depend on them.
Run `python -m pytest tests/ -q` after every task. Baseline at time of writing: 234 passed, 1 skipped, 19 xfailed.

Screens are lazily built, so a constructor error stays hidden until the screen is visited. After ANY screen edit, construct all 9 screens under all 4 themes — Appendix Z17 records six such defects that shipped because nobody did.

In PyQt6 an unhandled exception inside a reimplemented virtual (showEvent, paintEvent, resizeEvent) ABORTS THE PROCESS with no traceback. Never reference a widget attribute in one without a getattr guard. This exact bug (F002) took the whole app down.
No raw hex colour anywhere in ui/ outside ui/theme/. The contrast gate (tests/test_theme_contrast.py) must stay green.
do_not_regress: Inline setStyleSheet() calls outside ui/theme/ are at 59 against a target of 60 (Z17). Any new styling goes in the QSS, not inline.
Theme switch is ~245 ms with one screen built (Z18). Adding QSS bulk makes this worse — it is a known, accepted trade. Do not add per-widget stylesheets to 'fix' it.
tests/test_statement_package.py pins parser row counts (38/376/65/27), zero direction errors and IDFC control totals. Never loosen it.
verified_non_issues: Dialog modality: every dialog is opened with .exec(), which is application-modal. An isModal() probe before exec() returns False — that is expected, NOT a bug. Do not 'fix' it.
AccountDialog's 31 fields are organised across 5 tabs (Basic Info / Bank Details / Contact / Debit Card / Account Holders), not crammed into one pane.
AccountDetailsDialog's window title uses a proper em-dash. A mojibake character in console output was the terminal's cp1252 encoding, not the source.
The all-uppercase text in the PREVIOUS audit's screenshots was a zero-font fallback in that harness. This audit used real fonts; its captures are accurate.

already_fixed_in_this_pass.title: 7 of 9 screens rendered completely blank
already_fixed_in_this_pass.detail: DashboardScreen._navigate() guarded the placeholder swap with `if self._screen_pages.get(index) != screen:`, but _get_screen_page() populates that same cache before returning, so the condition was always False and stack.insertWidget() never ran. Accounts, Transactions, Fixed Deposits, Statement Import, Tax Documents, Tax and Settings all displayed an empty placeholder QWidget. Only Overview (built eagerly) and the error page (the one path that did not pre-cache) ever appeared.
already_fixed_in_this_pass.fix: Compare against what is actually in the stack — `self.stack.widget(index) is not screen` — and cache the error page in _get_screen_page() so the cache always reflects the stack.
already_fixed_in_this_pass.verified: All 9 screens now return their real class from stack.currentWidget() with 46-188 children each.

already_fixed_in_this_pass.title: Statement Import aborted the entire application
already_fixed_in_this_pass.detail: showEvent() -> _setup_selection_tab_order() referenced self.btn_ai_check, which was deleted when the AI controls moved to Settings. In PyQt6 an unhandled exception inside a reimplemented virtual calls abort() rather than propagating, so the process died with no traceback and exit code 127. This was MASKED by F001: while the placeholder was showing, the real screen never painted, so showEvent never fired. Fixing F001 exposed it.
already_fixed_in_this_pass.fix: Added _chain_tab_order(*names) which resolves widgets via getattr and skips missing ones.
already_fixed_in_this_pass.verified: Navigating to Statement Import no longer terminates the process.

already_fixed_in_this_pass.title: Income & Expectations crashed to an error page
already_fixed_in_this_pass.detail: _create_kpi_tile() named the value label `f"{object_name}_value"` (e.g. 'kpiExpected_value') while _update_kpi_tiles() read it back with findChild(QLabel, 'kpiValue'), returning None -> AttributeError. The screen the owner most asked for never loaded.
already_fixed_in_this_pass.fix: Both sides now use the objectName 'kpiValue'; the label also carries textrole='metric' so the QSS can style it.
already_fixed_in_this_pass.verified: Screen constructs with 97 children; _screen_errors is empty.

audit_findings.note: Every item below was observed in a real render or measured in code. Task ids that address them are given.

screen_motive.motive: Answer 'where do I stand' in one glance.
problems: The same four numbers appear TWICE: as KPI tiles (Total Balance / Income (FY) / Expense (FY) / Net Savings) and again in the 'Financial Summary' card below.
Bank balances appear THREE times app-wide: the Overview donut, the Overview 'Bank Accounts' card, and the Accounts screen bar chart.
KPI tiles are ~90px tall with content only in the top ~50px, and lay out 3+2 leaving a ragged gap.
'Interest Income ₹0.00' — see data_wiring F201.
The 'Bank Accounts' card scrolls at 3 of 5 rows inside a card with free space.

screen_motive.motive: Browse, filter and edit the ledger.
problems: The relocated Monthly/Categories chart takes ~500px; the table — the actual subject of the screen — gets ~150px and shows 3 of 10 rows.
Person / Account / FY appear in the top bar AND again in the screen's own filter row: four duplicated controls that can disagree.

Column widths are not content-aware: Mode shows 'Bank ...', Description 'INT AUTO REDEEM ...', Account 'Jana Small Finance ...', Person 'Pranav ...' — while 'Reference No' displays '—' in ~140px and a ~230px empty band sits after the last column.
A raw database 'ID' column is exposed to the user.

screen_motive.motive: Show expected income for the year against what actually arrived.
problems: 'Received to Date ₹0.00' and no Actual series on the chart, despite matching salary transactions existing in the FY — expectation-to-transaction matching does not run (F202).
FY and Person selectors are repeated ~60px below the identical top-bar selectors.
KPI values are bare label/value text with no tile container, while Overview's equivalents are bordered cards — two different KPI treatments in one app.
Every panel title is printed twice: once as a section heading and again inside the matplotlib figure.
X-axis reads 'Apr 1', 'May 1' — the day-of-month leaks into the month label.
A single-category donut renders '100.0%', which carries no information.

screen_motive.motive: Manage deposits and see interest by year.
problems: An empty ~490px chart panel reading '— No interest records found' occupies half the screen above the table.

SIX simultaneously filled toolbar buttons (Add FD, Delete Selected, Link Txn, Auto-Link, Recalculate Selected, Save Changes) — two greens with different meanings, three blues, and no single primary action.
'Expected Interest' and 'Actual Interest' are '—' on every row.
Person, Bank and FD No are all truncated ('Pranav ...', 'Jana Small ...', 'FD4522030...'), making FD No useless as an identifier, while Compounding and Method get generous width.
'Showing 4 fixed deposits.' is rendered in amber — a warning colour for neutral information.
A text hint ('Tip: Edit cells directly...') substitutes for a real affordance, and F2 does not actually enter edit mode on this table (F330).

screen_motive.motive: Get a bank statement into the ledger safely.
problems: The screen's 'Family Member' selector defaults to the SECOND person while the top bar says 'All Persons', and the Account list is consequently empty — the screen opens broken, and a mis-selection imports one person's statement into another's account.
Calls the same concept 'Family Member' where the top bar says 'Person'.
Field widths: two 1390px-wide combos beside a 90px Format select.
The drop zone is a flat grey band with no dashed border or icon, and 'Or Browse...' is right-aligned far from it.
~450px of empty card below the drop zone.
A disabled 'Back' button occupies space at step 1.

screen_motive.motive: Reconcile 26AS, AIS and TIS into one position.
problems: The three 'drop zones' are only a label plus a ~470px 'Select File' button — no drag-and-drop, unlike Statement Import which does have one. Two different file-input patterns in one app.
Four buttons that all do the same thing: three secondary 'Select File' plus one primary 'Upload Files' in the empty state.
The empty-state icon renders at ~16px and reads as a broken glyph.
~40% of the screen below the panel is dead space.
Section heading reads 'Salary_Pension Income' — a raw underscore in a user-facing label.
Sections collapse via a bare QCheckBox beside the heading. A checkbox means include/exclude, not expand/collapse; it is ambiguous whether unchecking removes that income from the computation.
Currency spinboxes are ~765px wide and ~44px tall for a rupee amount, so only ~5 fields fit per screen, and their 11px steppers sit at the far right edge.
Every empty field displays a formatted '₹ 0.00', so the user cannot tell which fields they have actually filled.
The right panel shows ~19 consecutive '—' rows, reading as broken rather than 'not yet calculated'.
The header says 'Please select a person from the top bar' while the top bar defaults to 'All Persons' — the screen is unusable until a global selector is changed.
The 'waterfall' has no visual encoding at all — no bars, no +/- signs, no grouping. It is a definition list.
A ~480px bar chart duplicates exactly the account cards beneath it (same 5 banks, same balances).
All bars share one teal colour while the Overview donut gives the same five accounts five different colours — two contradictory chart colour strategies.
A permanently reserved ~340x340px 'No account selected' detail panel squeezes the card grid into two cramped columns that then need their own scrollbar.
A green 'Active' pill on every card conveys nothing when every account is active.
Theme previews for Aurora vs Slate (and Nova vs Midnight Pro) are near-identical generic bar charts that do not communicate what differs.
Four ~190px preview cards in a ~1500px row leave ~700px empty.
'Manage Family' is indigo and the adjacent 'Manage Bank' is CYAN — same function, different colour, and cyan fails contrast under a white label.
Full-width ~660px buttons and ~610px password fields for short inputs.
Slowest navigation in the app at ~2.5s.

buttons.question: Are buttons needed, working, and is size/colour significant to function?
buttons.measured: 71 Theme.btn() calls: 33 secondary, 23 primary, 7 success, 5 danger, 2 edit, 1 hero.

specific_defects: Fixed Deposits shows six filled buttons at once, so nothing reads as the primary action and 'Delete Selected' (destructive) shouts as loudly as 'Add FD'.
Auto-Link and Save Changes are both green with unrelated meanings; Add FD, Link Txn and Recalculate are three similar blues.
Settings' 'Manage Family' (indigo) and 'Manage Bank' (cyan) do the same kind of thing in different colours.

Buttons stretch to their container: ~660px in Settings cards, ~470px for 'Select File'.
Disabled buttons (Edit/Delete on Transactions, Back on Statement Import step 1) occupy space with no hint that a selection is required.

dialogs.question: Is each dialog needed, or should it be a window / inline panel?

measured.verdict: keep as modal — short focused create/edit
TOO TALL — 805px is clipped on a 1366x768 display
borderline; 5 tabs inside a modal is heavy but organised
CONVERT — this is a list-management SCREEN wearing a dialog
CONVERT — same, and at 950px wide it is clearly a screen
CONVERT to the inline detail panel that already exists (and currently sits empty) on the Accounts screen

dialogs.principle: A modal is for a short decision that must finish before anything else. A list you browse, filter and act on repeatedly is a screen. The three 'Manage X' dialogs are reached from Settings, are 520-540px tall, contain tables and CRUD toolbars, and block the app while open.

data_wiring.claim: FD interest records are only created on two of three FD creation paths.
data_wiring.detail: allocate_fd_interest_to_fy() is called from ui/dialogs/fd_dialog.py (lines 490, 504) and ui/fixed_deposits_screen.py (line 720), but NOT from models.fixed_deposit.add_fd() itself, and NOT from the statement-import path (ui/statement_import_screen_modern.py calls add_fd_from_statement at line 167 with no allocation). Any FD created outside the dialog leaves FDInterestRecord empty, which zeroes Overview's 'Interest Income', the FD screen's Expected/Actual Interest columns, the FD Interest Runway chart, the TDS threshold panel and the Tax screen's FD interest.
data_wiring.note: Statement-created FDs are 'Pending Details' with a NULL maturity, so allocation would return early anyway — but the invariant should live in the model, not be re-remembered at each call site.
data_wiring.verified_by: Seeding 4 FDs via add_fd() left FDInterestRecord at 0 rows and get_total_fd_interest('2026-27') at 0.0.

data_wiring.claim: Expectation-to-transaction matching does not run, so 'Received to Date' is always ₹0.00.
data_wiring.detail: With 4 salary credits present in FY2026-27 and 12 monthly expectations seeded, the Income & Expectations screen reported Received ₹0.00, Still Expected = full ₹2,58,000, and rendered no 'Actual' bars. The screen's stated purpose — expected vs actual — is therefore unfulfilled.
data_wiring.investigate: models/income_expectation.auto_link_income_expectations() exists; determine whether it is ever invoked on refresh.

design_direction.brief: Colourful, attractive and interesting WITHOUT becoming decorative. In a financial tool, colour must mean something: the moment two buttons with different jobs share a colour, colour has stopped being information and become noise.
principles: COLOUR CARRIES MEANING. One accent for the primary action per screen. Semantic colour reserved for semantics: green = money in / positive, red = money out / destructive, amber = attention needed, blue/indigo = neutral action. Nothing else gets a fill.
DATA IS THE DECORATION. The interesting colour should come from charts and money figures, not from chrome. Delete decorative gradient banners; spend that colour on the numbers.
ONE IDEA PER SURFACE. If a number appears on a screen twice, one of them is wrong.
DENSITY WITH AIR. Financial users scan. Tighter rows and smaller inputs let more real data show, and whitespace goes between GROUPS rather than inside every control.
MOTION ONLY TO EXPLAIN. A 120ms ease on hover/expand is enough. No animation on data.
specific_moves: Give each of the 9 screens a distinct accent hue drawn from the theme's chart palette, used for its section headings and its single primary button. The app then feels colourful and each screen is instantly recognisable, without inventing per-screen palettes.
Money figures get a tabular-figures font feature and colour by sign (SUCCESS_TEXT positive, DANGER_TEXT negative) so a column of numbers reads at a glance.
KPI tiles get a large value, a small label, a sparkline and a delta chip — the same component on every screen.
Cards lose their heavy 1.5px borders in favour of a subtle shadow plus a 1px hairline, with a 3px left accent only where the card has a status.

sequence_rationale: F350 first so every later change is guarded by a render test — the three blockers fixed in this pass all hid behind lazy screen construction. Then the two data-wiring fixes, because several screens are being redesigned around numbers that currently do not exist. Then tokens, buttons and shared components, because every screen redesign consumes them. Terminology before screens so labels are written once. Charts and tables next. Then the dialog-to-screen conversions that stand alone (F340, F342). Screens last — with F341 placed immediately after F308, because moving account details into the side panel requires that panel to have been rebuilt first.

harness.purpose: Render every screen and dialog with REAL fonts and introspect them.
harness.critical: Without QT_QPA_FONTDIR the offscreen plugin exposes ZERO font families and Qt falls back to a capitals-only stub face, making every capture useless for typography. Assert QFontDatabase.families() is non-empty before drawing any visual conclusion.
pitfalls: Guard seed data on the ACCOUNTS table, not the persons table — a crash mid-seed leaves the person row behind and silently skips all later seeding, producing empty screens that look like app bugs.
Redirect config.DATA_DIR/DB_PATH AND core.database.DB_PATH/DATA_DIR — core.database captures them at import.
Do not call deleteLater() on a widget removed from a QStackedWidget; the PyQt wrapper and Qt both try to free it and the process segfaults. Keep a reference instead.
matplotlib builds its font cache on first import — discard the first timing measurement.
